cells.tense: You're tending it now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: Standing back far enough to see how it all fits
cells.ask: Offer this balance one thing to release — let a piece of the tending reach its own completion, and let the honoring come back to you as fulfillment rather than a letting-go.
cells.core:
You're tending what's yours to tend, and you're holding both sides of it at once — the part that needs more and the part that needs less — without forcing either. You can see how the whole thing fits together while you're still standing in the middle of it. That's the rare part: care and structure in the same pair of hands, neither one eating the other.

The care isn't exhausting you right now. That's how you know it's working.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending it with both hands, and the care isn't draining you.

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of it, bracing for a harvest that hasn't grown yet.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: Standing back far enough to see how it all fits together
cells.ask: Let one thing finish on its own timing — instead of managing the shape of what's coming, let something you've already lived through settle, and let the satisfaction of that be enough for now.
cells.core:
You're managing the whole pattern ahead of itself. Every part of it gets steered, shaped, adjusted before it's had a chance to grow into what it is — because somewhere ahead of you there's a version where it all works, and you're already living in that version. The watching has stopped being seeing. It's become holding on.

The irony is the tending is what's suffering. Not you — the thing you're trying to grow.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering the whole thing before it's had a chance to grow.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you, hands empty.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: Standing back far enough to see how it all fits together
cells.ask: Start small and keep at it — pick the nearest living thing, tend it badly, and let what you've kept going shine back at you. Don't push care into the empty place; just keep one thing growing and let that be the proof.
cells.core:
The seeing is still there — you know how it fits, you can spot the pattern across all of it — but the tending has gone quiet. Somewhere back there, caring for it stopped working, or cost too much, and you stepped away. The recognition didn't leave. The hands did.

You can still see the whole thing. You're just not in it anymore.
cells.sheetLine: You still see the pattern, but your hands have gone quiet.

cells.tense: You're already writing it — you just haven't signed your name to the page.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: Standing back far enough to see how it all fits together
cells.ask: Say out loud what you've already been tending — one thing you've kept alive that you'd call luck or circumstance. Let one person see the care that's already in it, and let the finishing of it be a release rather than a loss.
cells.core:
You've been tending something all along — you're doing it right now, as we speak, in how you hold the whole pattern and move things around to keep them growing. But you'd describe it as the situation being handled, or things staying on track. As though the care were happening to you rather than through you.

The stewardship is real. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending it. You just haven't claimed it.
